01 Admin Quickstart: Copilot CoE install

Run these steps one at a time in PowerShell 7. Keep the customer’s organization folder outside the kit folder; that way, updating the kit later will not overwrite the customer’s settings.

Two important rules:

  • For a brand-new install, do not use -ResumeExisting. It is only for finishing an interrupted install.
  • Before installing, configure Links.DataSafetyIncident with a real HTTPS link to an approved incident-reporting route. If you do not, the installer stops before it creates anything in the tenant.

Screenshot guide: The pictures below are from an internal content-demo tenant used to validate the kit, captured October 16, 2026. Red rectangles identify the affected areas. They do not mean every boxed area should be edited directly in SharePoint: follow the source-file and update instructions beside each picture.

Use the listed page or list path on your own CoE site. The pictures are embedded in this HTML file and remain available offline.

01Extract the kit and create the organization folder

First, choose where the customer’s organization folder will live. This folder controls the site’s wording, governance drafts, learning paths, and the starting prompts in the Copilot Prompt Library.

If someone already gave you a completed organization folder, copy that folder instead of creating a new one.

Customer typeFolder to copyPrompts included
Higher educationOrg-Template230 higher-education prompts, included by default
State/local government, commercial or GCC Moderate — not GCC High or DoDContentPacks\Government-StateLocal230 general government prompts; higher-education prompts are excluded

Use commands like this:

$installRoot = 'C:\CoE-Install\Contoso'
$kitRoot = Join-Path $installRoot '03_Build\CopilotCoE-Kit'
$orgPath = 'C:\CoE-Orgs\Contoso'

Set-Location $kitRoot

# Higher education:
Copy-Item .\Org-Template $orgPath -Recurse -Force

# Government — use this instead of the line above:
# Copy-Item .\ContentPacks\Government-StateLocal $orgPath -Recurse -Force

Then open the settings file:

notepad (Join-Path $orgPath 'Deployment-Settings.json')

In that file, set:

  • Tenant details.
  • The owner’s UPN.
  • The organization name.
  • The support mailbox.
  • The organization’s email domains.
  • Keep TeamVisibility set to Private.
  • Fill in real HTTPS addresses for Links.ServiceDesk, TechnologyRequest, AIGuidelines, and DataSafetyIncident.
  • For government deployments, replace every <placeholder> and set TimeZone — for example, Central Standard Time.

Optional: add the customer’s own prompts

The Prompt Library starts with the base prompts included in the folder you copied.

To add the customer’s own prompts, put CSV files here:

$orgPath\Content\OrgPrompts

Use the same CSV format used by the Microsoft 365 admin center:

Title,Description,Display Prompt,Prompt Text,Products,Department,Task Type,Locale

These are the same files you would upload through Copilot > Prompts > Import.

How the kit treats the files:

  • A new CSV file name adds new prompts.
  • A CSV with the same name as a base file replaces that base file.
  • An empty CSV with a base file’s name removes that base prompt set.
  • The kit does not modify your CSV files.

To turn off the Prompt Library entirely, set "PromptLibrary": "Off".

For the on-site location and an example of the environment-specific prompt sets, see the Prompt Library screenshot in step 05.

02Register or update the provisioning app

A person approved to consent to app permissions runs this once per tenant. Afterward, they should confirm in Entra that every required permission shows as Granted.

Set-Location $kitRoot

Install-Module PnP.PowerShell -RequiredVersion 3.2.0 -Scope CurrentUser

.\01_Register-CoEProvisioningApp.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath

Before moving on, check that the Entra app permissions are granted, including the delegated User.Read.All permission.

If consent changed after someone previously signed in, add -ForceAuthentication to the install command in the next step.

03Run the clean install

A SharePoint and Teams administrator runs this after the settings file and app consents are ready.

GCC Moderate / switching tenants: confirm the sign-in

When switching between commercial and GCC Moderate tenants, or when the browser offers the wrong cached account, add -AuthenticationMode Interactive -ForceAuthentication to the installer command below. Sign in with an approved administrator account for the target tenant.

-ForceAuthentication requests a fresh interactive sign-in; it is optional, not a GCC requirement. Also use it after app permissions or consent change. It does not select the tenant: confirm Tenant, AdminFQDN, SiteFQDN, and PnPClientID in the target organization’s Deployment-Settings.json first.

Do not combine -ForceAuthentication with -AuthenticationMode DeviceLogin. This kit supports commercial and GCC Moderate tenants, not GCC High or DoD.

Set-Location $kitRoot

.\02_Install-CopilotCoE.ps1 `
  -OrgPath $orgPath `
  -ContentMode Customer `
  -SeedDemoContent `
  -AcceptOrgAssets

-ContentMode Customer is the production setting: no demo disclaimer, no sample calendar events, and starting with 3.8.10, any org asset file named DEMO or SAMPLE is refused instead of hosted. Use -ContentMode Demo only for an internal sales/content-demo site, never for a customer-facing install. -SeedDemoContent is required either way — omitting it skips all page, catalog, and calendar content regardless of -ContentMode, leaving only the Team and an empty SharePoint site.

Using an organization-provided launcher? A short pwsh -NoProfile -File "Start-CoE-Install.ps1" command runs that launcher, which can pass the full argument list internally. Confirm that it calls 02_Install-CopilotCoE.ps1 with the intended -OrgPath, -ContentMode, -SeedDemoContent, and -AcceptOrgAssets. The launcher is not a different installer; no launcher is required for the direct command above.

A first install usually takes about 25–35 minutes. Creating the 230 base prompts accounts for roughly 5–10 minutes of that.

For a clean install:

  • Do not add -ResumeExisting.
  • For a fresh sign-in, follow the red callout above. If the Team/site was already created before a failure, follow the recovery steps below; -ForceAuthentication does not make another clean install safe.

If the install fails

Do not immediately start another clean install, and do not automatically delete or purge resources.

  1. Read the transcript files here: 
    $orgPath\RevisionAudit\*-transcript.txt
  2. Fix the underlying problem.
  3. Confirm that the existing Team and SharePoint site have the exact intended identity.
  4. Only then use -ResumeExisting to finish that same build.

If you are validating a changed version of the kit, use a new site alias or perform a separately reviewed removal and fresh install. Using -ResumeExisting does not prove that a new kit version works.

04Check the result

The install is not finished until this check passes. This script reads the site; it does not change anything.

Use the site address printed at the end of step 03.

$siteUrl = 'https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/CopilotCoE'

Set-Location $kitRoot

.\Test-CoEInstall.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -SiteUrl $siteUrl -ContentMode Customer

Always pass -ContentMode Customer here to match the install — it unlocks the Customer-mode checks (no sample rows, no demo text, and the Home “No sessions scheduled yet” placeholder when the calendar is empty). Omitting it silently skips those checks instead of failing them.

You are done when the final line says:

ALL CHECKS PASSED

If any line says FAIL, it names the problem. Send that output, along with the run log, to whoever is troubleshooting the install.

05Before readers see it

Before opening the site to regular users:

  • Add at least one non-owner test account as a member or reader, then do acceptance testing as that user.
  • Approve and feature one Agent Showcase entry so you can test both the empty and populated reader layouts.
  • Open Prompts in the site menu and confirm the Organization prompt library shows the prompts for that environment. Government sites must not show higher-education prompts.
  • To add or remove a catalog reviewer, edit the CoE Catalog Reviewers SharePoint group. You do not need to rerun a script for that.

Reviewer-group illustration: This demo did not have a CoE Catalog Reviewers group at capture time, so no group-management screenshot is shown. Do not use a different group as a substitute for the named reviewer group.

Use the update script only for reviewed changes:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope All

After any update, run step 04 again.

06Customizing content after install

There are several kinds of content, and they behave differently when the update script runs again. This matters because an edit made in the wrong place can either disappear during the next update or never apply at all.

When in doubt, edit the source file and rerun the update script. That is the safe approach, and it is the only method that survives future updates.

A. Single settings — AI policy URL, document list, org name, notice text

These include:

  • Links.AIGuidelines — the AI policy link shown in Service Catalog and Support and Governance.
  • GovernanceLinks — the bulleted “Official documents” list on the Governance page.
  • OrgName — your organization’s name in the welcome text.
  • OrgNoun — the word used for the organization, such as “company,” “agency,” or “university.”
  • SampleNotice — the notice or disclaimer text in the welcome content.

To change any of these, edit the settings file:

notepad (Join-Path $orgPath 'Deployment-Settings.json')

Change the value, save the file, then run:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope All
There is no SharePoint-native equivalent for these values. They are generated from the settings file every time. If you edit the rendered text directly in SharePoint, it will not stick; the next update rebuilds it from the setting.

B. Guide and section page wording

This covers pages such as:

  • “Start in 10 minutes.”
  • The Service Catalog table.
  • The Governance page body.
  • Other numbered section pages.

These pages are rebuilt from their source files on every run of 03_Update-CoEContent.ps1, no matter which -Scope value you use. There is no “preserve existing” option for this content.

A direct edit in SharePoint may work for now, but it will disappear the next time anyone runs the update script—even for an unrelated reason, such as adding a prompt or changing a setting.

To change this pageEdit this file
Start in 10 minutes$orgPath\Content\Guides\Guide-Start-in-10-Minutes.md
Service Catalog and Support, Governance and Responsible AI, and other numbered sections$orgPath\Content\Sections\<NN-Section-Name>.md

For “Start in 10 minutes,” create the override file if it does not already exist. Copy the kit’s version from SeedContent\Guides\ as your starting point.

For section pages, create or edit the override file under $orgPath\Content\..., matching the kit’s SeedContent\Sections\ path.

Then run:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope Guides

Or, to update everything:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope All
Do not hand-edit these pages directly in SharePoint and expect the change to last. If someone reruns the update later for any reason, SharePoint will silently replace your edit with whatever the source file says.

C. Governance Word documents

Governance documents behave the opposite way from guide and section pages.

By default, the update script preserves existing governance documents. It only replaces one when you explicitly pass -ReplaceFiles. When it does replace a file, it saves a before-copy in RevisionAudit.

To update a governance draft:

Edit the file under:

$orgPath\Content\Governance\...

Run:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope Governance -ReplaceFiles

A direct edit to the Word document itself—either in SharePoint or desktop Word—is also safe long-term. Without -ReplaceFiles, a future rerun leaves the document alone.

Why there is no Word screenshot here: the demo’s public Governance and Responsible AI files folder was empty at capture time. No draft has been invented or substituted. Open the actual governance Word draft in your deployment; do not edit the public Governance page or its “Official documents” list expecting that to change a Word file.

D. Home and the four captured vendor pages

These pages are special:

  • TrainingHome.aspx
  • Adoption-Best-Practices.aspx
  • Meet-your-ProjectTeam.aspx
  • Technical Readiness.aspx
  • Copilot-on-Microsoft-Mechanics.aspx

An ordinary rerun does not touch them.

They are rebuilt only when you explicitly pass -RepairCapturedPages. Use that switch deliberately, not as routine maintenance.

-RepairCapturedPages resets:

  • Home’s welcome text.
  • The Copilot tools tiles.
  • The four captured pages’ breadcrumbs.

It replaces direct SharePoint customizations to those specific elements with whatever the settings file and kit content generate.

If you want a permanent custom Home welcome message, set it through OrgName, OrgNoun, and SampleNotice in Deployment-Settings.json—the method described in section A. If you edit Home directly instead, a future -RepairCapturedPages run can silently replace your change.

Home: the Home screenshot in section A identifies the welcome elements. The demo did not render the Copilot tools tiles during capture, so there is no tile screenshot. In the four pictures below, only the red-boxed breadcrumb is being called out; the boxes do not imply that all other visible page content is regenerated from a setting.

E. Uploaded reference documents

Files placed in these folders are offered for hosting on every run:

$orgPath\Assets\Training
$orgPath\Assets\Service-Catalog
$orgPath\Assets\Agents
$orgPath\Assets\RAI-Policies

During a run, the script asks whether to host them. You can answer the prompt, or pass -AcceptOrgAssets to accept automatically.

In a Customer-mode install, a file whose name contains DEMO or SAMPLE (as a whole word) is refused automatically and never offered for hosting, even with -AcceptOrgAssets — rename it first if it is real organization content.

An already-hosted file is left alone unless you pass -ReplaceOrgAssets. Review the changed file first, then use that switch if you want the new version published.
